literal: Possession of the asset called excellence of the tongue, that excellence is not included in any other excellence.
translation: The possession of the asset called eloquence of the tongue is a unique excellence; that excellence is not to be found among any other excellences.
modern: நாநலம் என்று சொல்லப்படும் நன்மையைப் பெற்றிருப்பது ஒரு சிறந்த உடைமையாகும்; அந்த நன்மை வேறு எந்த நன்மைகளுள்ளும் அடங்குவது அன்று.
explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of eloquence, termed here as the 'excellence of the tongue' (நாநலம்). The author states that possessing this gift of speech is the greatest asset a person can have. He contrasts it with all other forms of goodness or wealth, asserting that this specific excellence stands completely apart and cannot be matched by any other virtues. The word 'யாநலத்து' refers to any other kind of excellence, emphasizing that eloquence is unparalleled in its power and utility.
